registryNote: Phase 1 ground truth for WAWU-Hub-API (branch feat/admin-surface). READ-ONLY for every later agent. Global route prefix is 'api/hub' (src/main.ts:28) — every `path` below is written WITHOUT that prefix; the wire path is /api/hub + path. Nothing in `endpoints`, `schema`, `auth` or `sideEffects` may be dropped, renamed, retyped, narrowed or widened.

frameworkProfile.language: typescript (TS ^5.7.3, ES2023 target, NodeNext module resolution — tsconfig.json)
frameworkProfile.layout: One directory per resource directly under src/, named kebab-case after the resource: src/<resource>/<resource>.module.ts + .controller.ts + .service.ts, with src/<resource>/dto/*.dto.ts, src/<resource>/guards/*.guard.ts (resource-local guards are the established idiom — CreatorAccountGuard is duplicated verbatim into 6 resource dirs rather than shared), and src/<resource>/tests/<resource>.contract.spec.ts. Cross-cutting code lives in src/common/{auth,guards,filters,interceptors,decorators,dto,prisma,types}. Every module is imported explicitly into src/app.module.ts's `imports` array — registration ORDER MATTERS (see the load-bearing comment at src/app.module.ts:90-98: PartnerServiceController's @Get(':id') catch-all swallows sibling routes if registered first).
frameworkProfile.adminTreePlacement: src/admin/<resource>/ per NestJS layout, registered as one module import line in src/app.module.ts. Route prefix must be 'admin/...' giving wire paths /api/hub/admin/...

orm.name: prisma
orm.config: prisma.config.ts; datasource url comes from DATABASE_URL env only (no url in schema.prisma)
orm.serviceWrapper: src/common/prisma/prisma.service.ts (PrismaService extends PrismaClient), exported by src/common/prisma/prisma.module.ts

frameworkProfile.validation: class-validator + class-transformer decorators on DTO classes in src/<resource>/dto/. Enforced by a single global ValidationPipe in src/main.ts:30-32 with { whitelist: true, forbidNonWhitelisted: true, transform: true } — an unknown body/query property is a 400, so admin DTOs must declare every accepted field. Param coercion uses Nest's ParseUUIDPipe (often `new ParseUUIDPipe({ version: '4' })`). Query pagination extends src/common/dto/pagination.dto.ts PaginationQueryDto (page/perPage, MAX_PAGE=1000, MAX_PER_PAGE=100, DEFAULT_PER_PAGE=20). One service validates by hand because it has no controller in front of it: src/credit-spend/credit-spend.service.ts:65-77.
frameworkProfile.authIdiom: Passport JWT. `@UseGuards(WawuAuthGuard)` (src/common/guards/wawu-auth.guard.ts — extends AuthGuard('wawu-jwt')) applied at CLASS level on almost every controller; extra role gates are stacked per-route as a second `@UseGuards(...)`. Claims are read with the `@CurrentUser()` param decorator (src/common/decorators/current-user.decorator.ts) which returns the raw WawuJwtClaims off req.user. There is NO roles decorator / metadata reflector anywhere — role checks are bespoke CanActivate classes. Three existing role-gate idioms: (1) CreatorAccountGuard — DB lookup of UserProfile.accountType==='creator', duplicated in 6 resource dirs; (2) env-allowlist admin guards (KycAdminGuard, VerificationAdminGuard) reading ADMIN_WAWU_USER_IDS; (3) AdminKeyGuard — shared x-wawu-admin-key header, src/common/guards/admin-key.guard.ts.
frameworkProfile.errorShape: Produced in exactly ONE place: src/common/filters/all-exceptions.filter.ts (registered globally at src/main.ts:33). Wire shape on every error: {"statusCode": <int>, "message": <string>, "data": null}. class-validator arrays are collapsed to their FIRST message (filter lines 80-83). Prisma P2002 -> 409 'That record already exists.'; P2025 -> 404 'Not found.' (PRISMA_ERROR_MAP, lines 21-35). Unmapped throwables -> 500 'Something went wrong. Please try again.'. No controller or service ever hand-rolls an error body.
frameworkProfile.successShape: Produced in exactly ONE place: src/common/interceptors/response.interceptor.ts (registered globally at src/main.ts:34). Plain return value -> {"statusCode":200,"message":"OK","data": value ?? null}. A service returning the Paginated<T> shape {items,currentPage,perPage,total} -> {"statusCode":200,"message":"OK","data": items, "pagination":{currentPage,nextPage,perPage,total}}. NOTE: statusCode in the BODY is hardcoded 200 even when the HTTP status is 201 — do not 'fix' this, the shipped app parses it. Types in src/common/types/shared.type.ts.
frameworkProfile.paginationConvention: Offset. `?page=&perPage=`. Some legacy list endpoints use OptionalPaginationQueryDto + paginateArray() and return a BARE ARRAY when neither param is supplied (backwards compatibility) — see src/common/dto/pagination.dto.ts:31-84. Affected: GET /services, GET /services/mentors, GET /learn/courses, GET /learn/guides, GET /verification/submissions.

testing.runner: jest ^30 + ts-jest, config inline in package.json (rootDir 'src', testRegex '.*\\.spec\\.ts$')
testing.style: Black-box HTTP contract tests. Each spec sets process.env.DATABASE_URL to wawu_hub_test BEFORE any import, builds a real Nest app with Test.createTestingModule importing only that resource's module + PrismaModule + WawuAuthModule + ConfigModule, re-applies the global ValidationPipe/AllExceptionsFilter/ResponseInterceptor by hand, then drives it with supertest. Real RS256 tokens are minted by logging in against the local mock WAWU ID on :4001 (mock-wawu-id/server.js), which the spec spawns if the port is cold. Fixtures use fixed UUIDs (00000000-0000-4000-8000-00000000000N for seeded users) and are swept in afterAll.
testing.command: npm run test:contract  (pins --runInBand --forceExit; the suite is NOT parallel-safe — README.md:5-30)

dataSources.honestCaveat: THERE IS NO PRODUCTION DATABASE REACHABLE FROM THIS ENVIRONMENT. Every shape below is measured from dev/test data. Counts are therefore small and the shape SET may be incomplete — but every shape listed WAS observed, so each is a fact, and law 8 applies to all of them. Where a validator admits a shape the data has not yet produced, that is called out as `admittedByValidator` and MUST also be tolerated.

identityFormats.note: **THE MOST DANGEROUS COLUMN IN THIS INVENTORY.** Phone is WAWU ID's non-null login identifier and the only human-typeable handle on a user. Across the two identity databases it holds FIVE distinct shapes for what is meant to be one identity. An admin 'find user by phone' that searches only '+234...' silently reports 11 of 15 real dev users as nonexistent, and that failure renders in the UI as an empty result, never as an error (law 8). Every admin lookup MUST build a variant set from the incoming value and match all of them; normalizing the stored values is FORBIDDEN (law 3 — this is a protected surface owned by another service). Shape counts merged across wawu_id_dev (15 rows) and wawu_id (3 rows).
identityFormats.alsoNotObserved: 0XXXXXXXXXX (11 chars, the local format a Nigerian user actually types) has not appeared yet but is the obvious sixth shape — tolerate it too.
identityFormats.ownedBy: WAWU ID (external identity service). READ-ONLY. Never write, never migrate.

shapes.validator admits +234XXXXXXXXXX, 234XXXX: 0 rows in dev/test — the table is empty

identityFormats.note: MIXED BY CONSTRUCTION. The DTO regex is ^(\+?234|0)[789][01]\d{8}$ (src/health-plan/dto/health-plan.dto.ts) — it accepts three spellings and stores whichever was typed. WellaHealth keys the enrollee on this value, so it is a real identity column. No rows exist yet, so an admin lookup that assumes one spelling will start failing the moment the first three users sign up. Treat as mixedFormat now, not later.

**MIXED FORMAT ON THE APP'S ROUTING KEY.** The schema calls slug 'a stable routing key... the app used to match services by name, which broke silently'. In wawu_hub_dev three of eight rows have slug == id (a UUID). In wawu_hub_test the SAME three rows instead hold 'seed-cac' / 'seed-nepc' / 'seed-trademark'. So one logical service is spelled three different ways across environments, and NEITHER database contains a row with slug 'cac' or 'nepc'. Any admin lookup/filter/link on slug must tolerate: a word slug, a 'seed-'-prefixed slug, and a raw UUID.

MIXED FORMAT, and the API CANNOT REPRODUCE what is stored. UpdateUserProfileDto validates handle against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_.]+$ (src/user-profile/dto/update-user-profile.dto.ts) — hyphens are REJECTED — yet 2 of 3 populated handles contain a hyphen (written by prisma/seed.ts). Dots and underscores are permitted by the validator but absent from the data. An admin handle search must accept hyphens, dots, underscores and mixed case, and must treat a null handle as normal (10 of 13 rows).
alsoTolerate: leading/trailing whitespace is not stripped anywhere

auth.summary: This backend is a PURE RESOURCE SERVER. It never issues, refreshes, or stores a user token. Every route keys on the JWT `sub` claim only.

sso.identityBackend: WAWU ID — /workspace/projects/WAWU-ID (NestJS, branch main). EXTERNAL AND PROTECTED. Never called except through the two clients below, never modified.
sso.tokenType: RS256 JWT, verified against WAWU ID's JWKS endpoint. jwks-rsa caches keys 24h (cacheMaxAge), rateLimit 5 req/min.
validationFiles: /workspace/projects/WAWU-Hub-API/src/search-response/guards/optional-wawu-auth.guard.ts (same strategy, degrades to anonymous instead of 401)
sso.jwksUrl: env WAWU_ID_JWKS_URL, fallback 'http://localhost:4001/.well-known/jwks.json'. Served by /workspace/projects/WAWU-ID/src/jwks/jwks.controller.ts (@Controller('.well-known') @Get('jwks.json')). kid is the RFC-7638 thumbprint of the RS256 public key.

expectedClaims.sub: string — the WAWU ID user id (uuid v4). THE ONLY thing this backend keys on.
expectedClaims.trustScore: number | null (CLAUDE.md says Trust Score does not exist in this product, yet it is on the token and is echoed by GET /users/me)
expectedClaims.platformRefs: optional { wawuafricaAppUserId?, onboardingRef?, beautyUserId?, basketUserId? } — DECLARED but NULL for all 15 dev users, and read by no Hub code

sso.issuerCheck: OPTIONAL and CURRENTLY OFF. wawu-jwt.strategy.ts only applies an `issuer` constraint when env WAWU_ID_JWT_ISSUER is set — it is absent from .env and .env.example. On the issuing side, WAWU ID stamps `iss` only when its own env JWT_ISSUER is set — also absent from /workspace/projects/WAWU-ID/.env. So no issuer is emitted and none is checked.
sso.audienceCheck: OPTIONAL, CURRENTLY OFF, AND UNSATISFIABLE. wawu-jwt.strategy.ts would enforce `aud` if WAWU_ID_JWT_AUDIENCE were set — but WAWU ID's TokensService.issueTokens (/workspace/projects/WAWU-ID/src/auth/tokens.service.ts:76-82) has no audience option at all and never emits an `aud` claim. Setting WAWU_ID_JWT_AUDIENCE on the Hub would reject 100% of real tokens.
sso.securityConsequence: With neither iss nor aud enforced, the Hub accepts ANY RS256 token signed by WAWU ID's key. WAWU ID signs for several products (Basket, Beauty, this hub) — the strategy's own comment (lines 22-26) names this risk. It also signs REFRESH tokens with the same key and no distinguishing claim beyond {sub, jti, type:'refresh'} (tokens.service.ts:84-91), and passport-jwt checks only signature + expiry, so a refresh token satisfies every Hub guard with req.user.sub populated. PROTECTED SURFACE — record, do not touch; the admin pipeline must not 'fix' this.

outboundServiceToService.note: Dev fallback key 'dev-internal-service-key-not-secret' is a publicly known string; the client throws at construction in NODE_ENV=production if the real key is unset. PROTECTED.

outboundServiceToService.target: /workspace/projects/WAWU-ID/src/auth/internal.controller.ts:164 — EXISTS, but it accepts mode ∈ {'hard','anonymize'} ONLY and 400s on anything else (internal.controller.ts:172-174).
outboundServiceToService.note: BROKEN CONTRACT: 'soft' is not a valid mode, so this call always 400s. AccountService catches and swallows the failure (account.service.ts:25-34) and returns a fabricated deletionScheduledAt regardless. The correct call for a grace period is POST /internal/users/:userId/mark-deletion (internal.controller.ts:190). PROTECTED SURFACE — report, do not repair here.

adminAuthToday.verdict: THERE IS NO ADMIN IDENTITY. No AdminUser table, no admin login, no admin token, no roles decorator. Three interim mechanisms exist and ALL THREE ARE UNREACHABLE in every checked-in configuration:

mechanisms.name: KycAdminGuard / VerificationAdminGuard
mechanisms.mechanism: env allowlist ADMIN_WAWU_USER_IDS (comma-separated wawuUserIds) checked against the verified JWT sub
mechanisms.status: UNREACHABLE — ADMIN_WAWU_USER_IDS appears in .env: NO, .env.example: NO, README: NO. Its only occurrences in the repo are two spec files that set it via process.env. Empty allowlist ⇒ 403 for everyone.

mechanisms.name: AdminKeyGuard
mechanisms.mechanism: shared secret in the x-wawu-admin-key header, constant-time compared to env WAWU_ADMIN_KEY; fails CLOSED when unset
mechanisms.status: UNREACHABLE — WAWU_ADMIN_KEY appears nowhere but that guard's own source. Guards POST/PATCH /learn/guides and PATCH /learn/playbook, all of which 401 unconditionally.
mechanisms.guardComment: 'Replace with a proper role check when the dashboard has real accounts.' — that is this pipeline's job.

adminAuthToday.consequenceForPhase5: The new admin identity must be genuinely separate (law 5): own AdminUser table, own secret env var, own iss/aud, and cross-rejection asserted in both directions. It must NOT reuse ADMIN_WAWU_USER_IDS, must NOT reuse the x-wawu-admin-key header, and must NOT touch wawu-jwt.strategy.ts or WawuAuthModule.
adminAuthToday.namespaceHazard: WAWU ID already owns /admin/* on its own host (ProvisioningController, /workspace/projects/WAWU-ID/src/provisioning/provisioning.controller.ts:15). The Hub's admin routes live at /api/hub/admin/* so there is no collision, but a dashboard talking to both services must keep the base URLs distinct.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: Response DTOs ARE the Prisma models — adding a column widens a live response
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: Almost every wire type in src/common/types/*.type.ts is `export type X = XModel` re-exported straight from generated/prisma/models, and services return the whole row by spread. Therefore ANY new column added to an existing table automatically appears in that table's existing app-facing response — which law 3 defines as a breaking change for strict parsers. If an admin contract needs to annotate an existing entity, put the annotation in a NEW SIDE TABLE keyed by the entity id, never a nullable column on the entity.
protectedSurfaceHazards.evidence: src/common/types/*.type.ts (28 of 39 are bare model re-exports); src/content-piece/content-piece.service.ts:118 and src/community/community.service.ts:73 return by spread.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: Module registration ORDER in app.module.ts is load-bearing
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: PartnerServiceController is @Controller('services') with a @Get(':id') catch-all matched by Express registration order. MentorModule and ServiceApplicationModule MUST stay registered before PartnerServiceModule or GET /services/mentors and GET /services/applications 400 with 'uuid v4 is expected' (this shipped once and was caught live).

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: The success envelope hardcodes statusCode 200 even on 201 responses
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: ResponseInterceptor always writes statusCode: 200 into the body regardless of the HTTP status. The shipped app parses this. Do not 'correct' it, and make admin responses match.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: Five list endpoints return a BARE ARRAY unless paging params are supplied
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: GET /services, /services/mentors, /learn/courses, /learn/guides, /verification/submissions switch response shape based on whether page/perPage is present. A regression test must assert BOTH shapes.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: GET /creator/state can return a kycStatus value that is not in the ReviewStatus enum
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: creator-state.service.ts synthesizes the literal 'not_started' when kycStatus==='pending' and the user has no KycSubmission row. Clients typed against ReviewStatus see a fourth value. Admin views must tolerate it and must NOT write it back.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: GET /notifications double-wraps its envelope
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: NotificationsResponse.items is itself a complete {statusCode,message,data,pagination} envelope, which the global interceptor then wraps again. Unusual but shipped. Do not normalise.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: POST /learn/guides can NEVER succeed, even with the admin key configured
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: UpsertLearnGuideDto restricts kind to ['guide','playbook','export','compliance']; the Prisma GuideKind enum is (country|article|template). The two sets are disjoint, and the service casts `(dto.kind ?? 'guide') as never`. Every insert hits Postgres with an invalid enum literal. Both the supplied-kind and omitted-kind branches are broken.

protectedSurfaceHazards.title: CreatorEarnings mixes a credit COUNT into a naira-typed array
protectedSurfaceHazards.detail: streamBreakdown[] shares one `amount` key across content/tips/dm (naira) and community_credits (a raw count), and community_credits is excluded from total/payable/held. Law 13: admin must read this same definition, never compute a second one — and must render the credits entry as a count, not currency.

seedOnlyTables.note: Tables whose ONLY writer in the whole repository is prisma/seed.ts. Each has a fully-built read endpoint and a screen in front of it. Law 13: an admin surface must NOT invent a second definition of these numbers — where the app's number is itself a fake, that is a GAP for the human, never something admin quietly recomputes.

protectedRoutes.note: MONEY-01. Every Hub API route the live web app (wawuafrica) and the admin dashboard (wawu-dashboard) call today, with the auth each enforces and the status and response shape each returned on main when the list was locked. src/protected-routes/protected-routes.regression.spec.ts runs one test per entry, in this order: the probes are a scenario and later ones read ids earlier ones captured. Paths are written without the global prefix, like the rest of this file. Adding a route here is fine; changing or removing an entry, or re-locking, is an owner decision (docs/WORKFLOW.md section 9). How to run it against any branch: README, "Protected route suite".

web.how: Every apiFetch / apiFetchPaginated call under src/ at origin/main (src/lib/api/mocks excluded): literal paths, paths held in a variable, each verifyPath the payment-return page calls, and both methods where the method is chosen at runtime. Calls with baseUrl go to WAWU ID, not this backend. Re-extract and diff with scripts/protected-routes/extract-callers.py.

dashboard.how: Every ROUTES key (src/lib/api/contract/generated.ts) and OPS_ROUTES key (ops.generated.ts) at origin/main that a file outside src/lib/api/contract names, plus the /api/ops proxy's own GET /admin/auth/me. Re-extract and diff with scripts/protected-routes/extract-callers.py.

notProtected.note: Routes a client DECLARES but never calls today, so they are not protected. If a client starts calling one, it is added (scripts/protected-routes/extract-callers.py reports it).
notProtected.webCallsToWawuId: src/lib/api/auth.ts calls WAWU ID directly (/auth/register, /auth/login, /auth/email/verify/*, /auth/forgot-password, /auth/reset-password, /auth/refresh). Those are WAWU ID's routes, not this backend's.
